candidate-3.question: Which idea is candidate 3 (a build, not a subtraction; cutting is deferred)?

answer.rationale: Judged against the goal statement (Unix philosophy, compose via pipes) and the three picks. Dead = the job belongs to another tool or to a killed design; deferred = fits principle 1 but has no second concrete use yet.

answer.text:
Dead (never re-propose): citation edges (RFC-064 §2, pins replace them); globals / tag-selected docs in pack (session hook is the mechanism); graph query (--json + jq is the query language); graph diff (git + validate cover it); section sub-nodes (multiplies graph and data model for no agent leverage over show sections); agent-session store (abandoned daemon vision).
Deferred (revisit after Pins -> Trust -> Pack land): edge attributes (edge table exists since #99; add an attribute at two uses, context-tier override is the first candidate); status-gate invariants (validation rule; see whether stale-blocks-advance is the first gate); decision lineage (a supersedes walk over context); coverage projection (mostly covered by required edges; revisit if pins expose unowned code as the real question); graph export DOT/Mermaid (human leverage only, one output format when asked); reverse index beyond why <path> (waits for pin density).

dead-ideas.question: Which of the remaining ideas are dead (never re-propose) versus deferred (revisit after these three land)?

answer.rationale: User answered "unix philosophy". Principle 1 stands as the tiebreaker; the graph is legitimate only as small composable primitives emitting text/JSON, never as an engine that owns the workflow. Rules out anything that turns lazyspec into a platform.

answer.text:
Unix philosophy: lazyspec does one thing well (structured markdown and the typed graph its links form), emits text and JSON, and composes with other tools through pipes rather than absorbing their jobs.
Candidates are judged by: does this add a small primitive that emits data other tools can consume, or does it pull a neighbour's job (query engine, orchestration, search index) inside the binary? Principle 1 remains the tiebreaker. README "context engine" tagline should be read as "a source other tools pipe from", not a platform.

goal-statement.question: What is the one-sentence goal of lazyspec that the candidates are judged against — does the README "context engine" tagline win, convention principle 1 ("produce, validate, serve structured markdown") win, or a new graph-first statement replace both?

answer.text:
Agent leverage first (tokens saved and decisions improved per agent call), then build cost, then unblocking of other ideas. Constraint: each candidate's first slice must ship in at most three iterations.
Pre-filter under the unix test before ranking: pass = reverse index, export, diff, edge attributes, lineage, section anchors, context --pack, RFC-067 completion; borderline = coverage, status-gate invariants, staleness/trust (own data, but computed); fail = query language (jq exists), agent-session store (another tool's private state), semantic search.

selection-criteria.question: What ranks candidates: agent leverage per token, cost to build, unblocking of other ideas, or scope-fit against the goal statement — and in what tiebreak order?

intent: Prioritise and refine three candidates, drawn from the context-graph gap analysis and the ten follow-on ideas (code-to-doc reverse index, edge attributes, graph query, graph diff, decision lineage, status-gate invariants, section sub-nodes, coverage projection, agent-session store, graph export, plus RFC-064 pack/trust and RFC-067 completion), into a set ready to become RFC/story chains in this repo. The interview must decide what "context graph" means for lazyspec given convention principle 1, pick three, refine each to RFC-writable shape, and record which ideas are dead so they are not re-proposed.
